ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Three blocks $a$, $b$, and $c$ with gravitational forces $G_{a}=10\,\mathrm{N}$, $G_{b}=20\,\mathrm{N}$, and $G_{c}=30\,\mathrm{N}$, respectively, and two identical light springs $p$ and $q$ with spring constants of $500\,\mathrm{N/m}$ each, are connected by thin strings as shown in the figure. Block $a$ is placed on a smooth horizontal table. Initially, spring $p$ is at its natural length, and all blocks are at rest. A horizontal force is then applied slowly to the left end of spring $p$ until block $c$ just lifts off the ground. (The weights of the light springs and thin strings are negligible.)

1. What is the compression amount of the light spring $q$ at the beginning?
2. The height to which block $b$ rises during this process?
3. How much does the left end of the spring move to the left in the process $p$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows that block a is placed on a smooth horizontal tabletop; the left side of a is connected to a horizontal spring p, and the left end of spring p is pulled by a leftward external force F. The right side of a is connected to a thin rope; after the thin rope passes around a fixed pulley at the right end of the table, it vertically downward connects to block b. Below block b is connected vertical spring q; the lower end of spring q is in contact with/connected to block c, and c is located on the ground. Reasoning: The process is slow, so static equilibrium can be made respectively according to the initial and final states. It is known that the stiffness coefficients of the two springs are both k=500 N/m. 1. Initially spring p is at its natural length and has no horizontal elastic force on a; a is stationary on the smooth tabletop, so the tension in the rope T=0. For the force equilibrium of b: the upward elastic force of spring q on b equals the gravity of b G_b=20 N, therefore the initial compression amount x_{q0}=G_b/k=20/500=0.04 m=4 cm. 2. When c is just about to leave the ground, spring q must pull c upward, and the elastic force equals G_c=30 N, so at this time q is in a stretched state, with elongation x_{qf}=G_c/k=30/500=0.06 m=6 cm. b rises from the initial compressed 4 cm position to the final stretched 6 cm position, therefore the rising height of b is 4 cm+6 cm=10 cm. 3. In the final state, for the equilibrium of b: the upper rope tension T needs to balance the gravity of b 20 N and the downward pulling force of spring q on b 30 N, so T=50 N. For the horizontal equilibrium of a, the pulling force of spring p is also 50 N, therefore the elongation of p is x_p=T/k=50/500=0.10 m=10 cm. From the rope length constraint, when b rises 10 cm, a moves left 10 cm. The left end of spring p must further move left by 10 cm relative to a to produce this elongation, so the left end of spring p moves left in total 10 cm+10 cm=20 cm.
